items.title: 54270_Doc Cheatham oral history interview
items.q: So when the spot light hit me, on "Poor Little Rich Girl," and Tate, you know, he didn't even give you a smile, he just threw his stick over there and pointed

ctx.x: Cause I was new in Chicago, so I sat in the pit and they all treated me pretty bad, there. You know, and Erskine Tate's brother, which was a trumpet player, he was very nice, he was trying to show me the score, we had to play for picture also, and they had the scores thee and everything. And it wasn't very difficult, he was showing me everything, but the only problem came was when the feature -- the band had a feature, and they were playing, at that time, "Poor Little Rich Girl." That was the feature number of…

You see when Louie was there, the minute that spotlight hit Louie, man, on the "Poor Little Rich Girl" the people were screaming so much, you couldn't hear -- you couldn't hear what he was playing, half the time. Cause he was so great. So when the spot light hit me, on "Poor Little Rich Girl," and Tate, you know, he didn't even give you a smile, he just threw his stick over there and pointed like he didn't know that.

So I jumped up and started playing and, man, the house -- the spot light and the spot light hit me and the house screamed and screamed and after awhile you could hear -- you could just measure the -- the diminishing of the screams came right down to nothing and I'm up there playing like a fool.
